To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

in highly invasive melanoma and glioblastoma cells, the expression of a nonadhesive precursor form of N-cad herin (proNC AD) promotes tumor cell invasion, whereas the mature N-cadher in (NCAD) is not involved in invasion.

the ratio of proNCAD to mature NCAD on the surface of tumor cells correlates directly with invasion potential and that the expression of proNCAD, rather than the expression of mature NCAD, is a critical determinant of tumor cell invasion and metastasis.
in the most aggressive melanomas, brain tumors, and other tumors, precursor N-cad (proNCAD), an aberrantly processed nonadhesive form of N-cad, is present at the cell surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of cadherins in cancer metastasis.
understanding how the cadherin family of proteins, which are known to be involved in tumor metastasis, are regulated at the posttranslational level.
the role of the cadherin superfamily of cell adhesion molecules in tumor invasion and progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

in invasive tumor cells, pro-NCAD is expressed at the cell surface and promotes invasion and metastasis, whereas in non-invasive tumor cells, proNCAD is not expressed at the cell membrane and does not promote invasion.
proNCAD promotes tumor invasion by promoting cell migration and by preventing cell-cell adhesion.
proNCAD is a novel invasion-promoting molecule that is a potential therapeutic target for cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ratio of proNCAD to mature NCAD is an important determinant of the metastatic potential of tumor cells.
the ratio of proNCAD and NCAD on tumor cell surfaces correlates with invasion potential and that proNCAD promotes invasion.
aberrantly processed NCAD is a novel biomarker of invasive tumor cells, and that the relative ratio of mature to precursor NCAD is an indicator of tumor cell motility.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the ratio of proNCAD to mature NCAD at the cell surface is the key to invasion, and that the presence of both moieties at the cell surface does not necessarily mean that mature NCAD will be the predominant form.
in the most aggressive tumor cells, the cadherin N-cadherins are processed differently, resulting in the surface expression of a nonadhesive, pro-invasive isoform, proNCAD.
in the most malignant tumor cells, the cadherin switch from E-cadherin to N-cadherins, a hallmark of tumor progression, is not complete.
